findings.title: Client calls `res.json()` on a 204 No Content response, causing the mutation to always fail
findings.rationale: The server returns HTTP 204 with no body. `fetch`'s `res.json()` on a 204 response rejects with a SyntaxError because the body is empty. The mutation will never succeed, so the button click has no effect and the UI shows a pending/error state. This breaks the feature for every caller (the FindingsPanel component).

findings.title: Client does not surface server errors as `ApiError`
findings.rationale: The `mutationFn` uses raw `fetch` and does not check `res.ok`. On a non-2xx response (e.g. 404, 500), it will attempt `res.json()` and either throw a generic `SyntaxError` (if the error body is not JSON) or return the error body as success data. This violates the project convention that all client requests surface errors as `ApiError` (see `client/src/lib/api.ts:44-58`). Users will see a generic error message and lose the server's error code and details.

findings.title: Client mutation does not surface errors as `ApiError`
findings.rationale: On a non-2xx response, the code calls `res.json()` and returns the error body as data. This causes the mutation to treat an error as success, passing the error body to `onSuccess` and invalidating queries. The user never sees the error. Per rule 3, all client fetch calls should throw `ApiError` on non-2xx responses.

findings.title: Client mutation calls `res.json()` on a 204 No Content response, causing the mutation to throw on success
findings.rationale: The server returns 204 with no body. `res.json()` on an empty body throws a `SyntaxError`. The mutation rejects, `onSuccess` never runs, and the query invalidation that refreshes the findings panel is skipped. The feature is completely broken on the happy path.

findings.title: Client mutation returns error body as data on non-2xx responses instead of throwing ApiError
findings.rationale: Per the project's house rules (rule 3), client code that calls `fetch` directly must throw an `ApiError` on non-2xx responses. The current code calls `res.json()` unconditionally, so on an error response it returns the parsed error body as the mutation's data. This causes `onSuccess` to run even when the request failed, incorrectly invalidating the reviews query and losing the error status and code.

matched_title: Client mutation uses raw fetch without ApiError handling and parses JSON from 204 response

findings.title: Client mutation uses raw fetch without ApiError handling and parses JSON from 204 response
findings.rationale: The new `useDismissAllSuggestions` mutation calls `fetch` directly and, on success, calls `res.json()` on a 204 No Content response (which has no body). This will either return `undefined` or throw a parse error. More importantly, on a non-2xx response the function does not throw an `ApiError` as required by the repository's house rule (rule 3). The existing `apiFetch` utility in `client/src/lib/api.ts` handles both cases: it throws `ApiError` on errors and returns the parsed body only when appropriate. The mutation should use `apiFetch` or replicate its error handling.

findings.title: Client copy of shared contract not updated
findings.rationale: Rule 2 of api-contract-house-rules: a shared contract change in `server/src/vendor/shared/` must also be applied to `client/src/vendor/shared/` in the same diff. The `merge_conflict` field is added to the server copy but the client copy (`client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/platform.ts`) is left unchanged. The two copies will silently diverge; the client will not know about the new field and may fail to parse responses that include it, or the server may reject requests that omit it. The field is additive and optional, so no deployed caller breaks today, but the drift is a maintenance hazard.
